stories.headline: Massive unrest and clashes erupt across France over living costs
stories.body:
French authorities said about 550,000 demonstrators joined cost-of-living protests across the country on Saturday. The nationwide demonstrations brought together trade unions, school students, and the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement.

Clashes between protesters and police led to two deaths during the unrest. A 22-year-old police officer died in Nantes after being struck by a vehicle. A protester also died near Paris. French authorities reported around 2,400 arrests across the country after the violence. Police in Paris reported a record 855 arrests in the capital alone. France's interior ministry said almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes were injured during Saturday's unrest. Seven of those injured officers were hurt seriously. On Sunday, police fired tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered at Place de la République in Paris.

Violent incidents occurred in several other parts of France during the demonstrations. An apparent arson attack damaged a 19th-century town hall in the city of Limoges on Saturday. Firefighters fought the town hall blaze through Saturday night and into Sunday morning. Limoges Mayor Guillaume Guérin said municipal police ran out of ammunition around 3:30 p.m. while trying to hold off rioters. Guérin called the incident a colossal failure of the state.

French President Emmanuel Macron gave a televised address on Sunday. Macron blamed radical far-left factions and criminal elements for the destruction during the protests. Macron said that those who destroyed must pay. He said that those who looted must pay back. He added that those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable.

International figures also commented on the situation in France. US President Donald Trump posted on social media and blamed immigration for the unrest. Trump said that France is burning. Protests over the cost of living and public services were not limited to France. Similar demonstrations also took place in Spain, Italy, and Portugal.

stories.headline: Deadly fire at Canadian military base kills four during training
stories.body:
Four Canadian service members died on Saturday during a military training exercise in Alberta. A fast-moving fire and explosion occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright. Soldiers were conducting live-fire combat exercises when a grass fire started about 1 kilometer away. Major-General Wade Rutland said uncommonly strong winds pushed the fire toward the range administrative area.

The four deceased service members were identified as Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding, and Pte Hayden Lykkemark. Hospitals admitted 39 patients, with at least 19 in critical condition. Internal military communications said 31 people were very seriously injured, according to the Globe and Mail.

Alberta's health agency sent 30 units to Wainwright, including 22 ground ambulances, six planes, and two helicopters. Military medical personnel parachuted into Wainwright shortly before midnight to assist. Ontario mayoral candidate Cathy Keane said on Facebook that her eldest son was among the critically injured personnel.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the incident one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime. Carney ordered flags on all federal buildings across Canada to be flown at half-mast. The Department of National Defence said there were no indications that the fire was a terrorist attack. Canadian Forces Base Wainwright usually has about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers on site daily.

The four deceased service members were identified as Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding, and Pte Hayden Lykkemark.
Internal military communications indicate that 31 people were very seriously injured in the fire, according to the Globe and Mail.
Alberta's provincial health agency deployed 30 units directly into Wainwright, including 22 ground ambulances, six fixed-wing planes, and two helicopters.
Military medical personnel parachuted into the town of Wainwright shortly before midnight to help respond to the disaster.
Cathy Keane, an Ontario mayoral candidate, stated on Facebook that her eldest son was among the critically injured military personnel.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime."
Prime Minister Mark Carney ordered flags on all federal buildings across Canada to be flown at half-mast.
The Department of National Defence stated there were no indications that the fire at CFB Wainwright was a terrorist attack.
Canadian Forces Base Wainwright typically has about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers on site on a given day.

stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in occupied West Bank
stories.body:
Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats and Palestinian civilians near Taybeh on Saturday. The targeted delegation included Belgian, French, and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor. Eyewitnesses said an attacker aggressively shouted "France, France" before pushing French Mayor Bernard Baudoux to the ground. Settlers smashed a reinforced window of an SUV carrying European diplomats as the vehicle drove away.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military blamed Israeli rioters for the attack. The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted a statement titled "Serious accusations require serious evidence" casting doubt on the accounts. On Friday, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was hospitalized after an assault while covering a Palestinian olive harvest. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called for Levine's attackers to be jailed before attending a settler conference on Sunday.

US diplomats including Assistant Secretary of State Riley Barnes and US Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch visited Taybeh on Sunday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing crisis in the West Bank. Human rights group Yesh Din recorded at least 170 settler attacks on Palestinians since September 27. The West Bank is home to about 500,000 Israeli settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians.

stories.headline: Trump pauses tariffs on nations buying Russian crude energy
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump paused sanctions linked to Russia two days before they were scheduled to take effect. Trump invoked Section 115 of the Graham Act to certify that waiving sanctions was in the US national interest. The Graham Act duties included tariffs of up to 500% on Russian goods. They also included tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest importers of Russian crude oil. According to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, China receives about 50% of Russia's crude exports, while India receives about 37%.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump's 60-day waiver decision. Rubio said India has voluntarily diversified its energy portfolio but still depends substantially on Russian energy. Trump posted on Truth Social that his decision was aimed at avoiding driving Russia away from peace negotiations. Trump also temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel to allow fuel into global markets and lower prices.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the order an important and truly historic moment. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told NBC News that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a historic mistake.

stories.headline: Protests erupt in India over voter roll revisions and election official
stories.body:
Protesters staged widespread demonstrations in India against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after a voter roll investigation. Protests began following a September 23 investigation regarding Election Commissioners' objections to roll revisions. Civil society organisations including Jan Sarokar, MKSS, Voter Adhikar Manch, and NFIW held a Jan Sunwai public hearing in Batla House.

A public audit of 258 households in Delhi's Okhla constituency found over 100 voters wrongly classified. The audit showed these voters were marked as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate. In the Okhla constituency, over 67,000 names were placed on the notice list out of 1.85 lakh draft roll voters. Nearly 1.6 lakh names in Okhla were placed on the ASDD list.

Political groups and police clashed during related demonstrations. Delhi Police registered three FIRs against protesters for violating prohibitory orders, conducting a flag march, and obstructing police officers. CRPF Director General GP Singh commended a female CRPF officer for demonstrating restraint after being slapped during a Cockroach Janta Party march. Mumbai Police detained several people at Carter Road in Bandra who gathered for a Tiranga March called by the Cockroach Janta Party.

Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14. Das and Ranka were detained after scaling locked gates at Jantar Mantar. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke accused authorities of using delaying tactics to prolong the detention of Das and Ranka.

In a related digital rule development, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory on October 10 asking Meta to review its content recommendation systems. Apar Gupta of the Internet Freedom Foundation criticized the MeitY advisory, calling it a continuing censorship directive.

stories.headline: Actor Tiger Shroff unhurt after gunfire incident in Mumbai
stories.body:
Unidentified assailants opened fire near actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai on Sunday evening. The shooting occurred at around 7:00 PM near Pushpa Park in Juhu outside a football club. Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde said five rounds were fired during the incident. Shinde visited Shroff's residence on Sunday night.

Shroff suffered injuries to his left hand from gunpowder and glass shards during the firing. His driver Firdaus sustained a hand injury, and auto-rickshaw driver Chauhan was also injured. Gangster Anil Pandit posted that he and Harman Sandhu carried out the attack to teach Shroff a lesson. A video featured Anil Pandit claiming the Lawrence Bishnoi gang targeted Shroff for working with actor Salman Khan.

Lawrence Bishnoi has been in prison since 2015 and is currently in a Gujarat jail. Anmol Bishnoi was arrested in California in November 2024 and deported to India in November 2025.

stories.headline: Tragic stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal kills at least 17
stories.body:
A deadly stampede occurred at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata on Saturday evening. Reports gave different casualty figures for the incident. The Hindustan Times reported that at least 19 people were killed and 25 were injured. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari reported that at least 17 people were killed, including a seven-year-old girl. The stampede happened at around 7:40 PM during Saptami celebrations amid sudden rainfall.

Police are examining video footage capturing a microphone warning that the Chorbagan pandal was in poor condition and might collapse. Local residents in Chorebagan started rescue efforts and carried injured victims to cabs to reach Calcutta Medical College and Hospital.

Chief Minister Adhikari announced a Special Investigation Team headed by a sitting or retired High Court judge to probe the stampede. Police arrested seven people under charges dealing with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The West Bengal government announced a ₹25 lakh ex-gratia payment and a Group D job for the next of kin of each deceased victim. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ₹2 lakh compensation from the PMNRF for families of the deceased and ₹50,000 for each injured person. Kolkata Police Commissioner Ajay Kumar Nand imposed Section 163 prohibitory orders on roads adjoining the pandal until October 20. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were also imposed in parts of Bowbazar until Tuesday.
